destination.title: Finiteness, information and geometry of theory spaces
destination.question: How can theory spaces and effective descriptions be organized or constrained through tame geometry, descriptive complexity and information, and where do quantum-gravity consistency conditions enter?
destination.summary: A coherent organizing region is available, provided qualitative tameness, quantitative complexity, statistical learnability, metric geometry and UV consistency remain distinct targets. The original numerical membership is useful retrieval provenance, not evidence of their equivalence.

systems: Effective theories considered for quantum-gravity completion
Scalar field spaces and moduli spaces
targets: Definability of theory spaces and observables
Theory-space distances, limiting behavior and volume geometry
Adjacent questions about scalar constraints and EFT validity
regimes: Source-specific perturbative, exact and asymptotic settings
Fixed finite cutoff for the stated gravitational tameness and global complexity conjectures
Finite-distance singularities distinguished from infinite-distance limits
assumptions: Quantum-gravity tameness and finite-complexity statements remain conjectures.
Ordinary QFT results do not require quantum-gravity completion merely because they share this family.
Different physical restrictions apply to CFT spaces, gravitational EFTs and particular exact observables.
conventions: Descriptive complexity, computational complexity and statistical sample complexity are different notions.
Information distance and scalar kinetic distance require explicit normalization before comparison.
Tameness of a continuous space is not a claim that it contains finitely many points.
Dimensions, cutoff choices and metric conventions remain source-specific.
includes: Separate questions about tame spaces and tame observables
Navigation to alternate homes for model selection, quantum-information agendas and possifolds
excludes: A universal implication from any singularity to a vanishing quantum-gravity cutoff
Universal validity inferred solely from dimensional reduction
A theorem identifying all supplied complexity notions
Automatic promotion of outside-source probes to original numerical membership
Fine-question equivalence inferred from shared overview cards

sources.title: Spaces of Quantum Field Theories

evidence.text: How can theory space be defined so that distances, convergence, disconnected components, boundedness and the information required to specify a QFT become precise? The broader objective is classification beyond perturbative Lagrangian descriptions.

sources.title: The tameness of quantum field theory: Part I - Amplitudes

evidence.text: Can o-minimal definability provide a generalized finiteness principle for QFT observables, including singular limits, and how far does perturbative tameness extend to exact observables, RG flow, and effective theories compatible with quantum gravity?

sources.title: The Tameness of Quantum Field Theory, Part II -- Structures and CFTs

evidence.text: How can families of QFTs and their observables define logical structures, and which physical restrictions could make both CFT theory spaces and their observables o-minimal? The paper separately considers analogous conjectures for effective theories compatible with quantum gravity.

sources.title: Neural network learning and Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Does the proposed tame, o-minimal structure of quantum-gravity effective theories imply statistical learnability of their couplings and derived classification/regression problems, with finite training-sample requirements?

sources.title: Tame embeddings, volume growth, and complexity of moduli spaces

evidence.text: Can tame isometric embeddability explain compactifiability bounds on quantum-gravity moduli-space volume, strengthen them to every geodesic radius, and relate their coefficient to geometric complexity and duality identifications?

sources.title: Tame complexity of effective field theories in the quantum gravity landscape

evidence.text: Can sharp o-minimality quantify EFT complexity and unify quantum-gravity finiteness constraints through finite descriptions of individual EFTs and uniform bounds across the landscape at fixed cutoff?

sources.title: Tameness and Complexity in Quantum Field Theory and Gravity

evidence.text: Which physical functions are definable in o-minimal structures, when does sharp o-minimality give them finite descriptive complexity, and which physical conditions enforce these properties in QFT and quantum gravity?

sources.title: Spaces of Quantum Field Theories

evidence.text: State–operator correspondence and OPE factorization organize CFT observables into sequence-space data. Heat evolution suppresses high-dimension contributions; sewing pairs of pants relates OPE norms to genus-two partition functions and spectral terms to genus-one amplitudes.

sources.title: The tameness of quantum field theory: Part I - Amplitudes

evidence.text: Associate graph integrals with relative periods of auxiliary algebraic families. Algebraic maps relate momenta and masses to geometric parameters; resolution of singularities and homogenization enter the construction. Apply the imported definability theorem for relative periods.

sources.title: The Tameness of Quantum Field Theory, Part II -- Structures and CFTs

evidence.text: Test the framework through spectral sums, Wick contractions, special-function representations, conformal-block expansions and sphere free-energy asymptotics. For finite-state Euclidean quantum mechanics, finite spectral sums give observables in Rexp; the free-particle and oscillator examples also generate Rexp.

sources.title: Neural network learning and Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Represent hypothesis-induced sets as a fixed definable family of fibers S_w={v:(v,w)∈S}; use the non-independence property of o-minimal structures to obtain finite VC dimension, then invoke imported learning theorems.

sources.title: Tame embeddings, volume growth, and complexity of moduli spaces

evidence.text: Compare intrinsic and ambient balls: an isometric embedding puts the intrinsic radius-D ball inside the ambient radius-D ball while preserving its volume. Combining this inclusion with the tame-volume theorem gives the intrinsic growth bound.

sources.title: Tame complexity of effective field theories in the quantum gravity landscape

evidence.text: Encode infinite coupling expansions through finite differential systems or recursion relations. Examples use Pfaffian chains, Log-Noetherian functions, exact zero-dimensional integration, and Seiberg–Witten differential relations. Exact RG equations are explored as a possible extension.

sources.title: Holographic origin of TCC and the distance conjecture

evidence.text: What boundary information is required to distinguish a bulk effective theory and its interactions?

sources.title: On the complexity of quantum field theory

evidence.text: How can one quantify the information needed to specify QFT actions and observables, detect simpler representations, and characterize changes under perturbation theory, exact limits and renormalization?

sources.title: On the Geometry of the String Landscape and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which geometric restrictions distinguish continuous moduli spaces of consistent quantum gravity from those of nongravitational field theories, and what constraints follow for effective theories, inflation and axions?

sources.title: Infinite Distances and Factorization

evidence.text: What physics generates infinite information-metric distances, how does it differ from quantum criticality, and can factorization explain the behavior described by the Swampland Distance Conjecture?

sources.title: Dimensional reduction and (Anti) de Sitter bounds

evidence.text: Can dimensional reduction distinguish ambiguous order-one parameters in conjectured quantum-gravity bounds?

sources.title: The zoo plot meets the swampland: mutual (in)consistency of single-field inflation, string conjectures, and cosmological data

evidence.text: Which proposed restrictions distinguish scalar effective theories admitting quantum-gravity completion from theories in the swampland?

sources.title: The Swampland: Introduction and Review

evidence.text: How can quantum gravity constrain an effective theory below its apparent cutoff? A Swampland scale indicates when modification becomes necessary for eventual completion, even when no immediate inconsistency occurs at that energy.

sources.title: Taming the landscape of effective theories

evidence.text: Can finiteness of quantum-gravity-compatible effective theories be implemented as a structural requirement that their parameter spaces, scalar field spaces, and coupling functions form tame, o-minimally definable geometry?

sources.title: Strengthening the de Sitter swampland conjecture in warm inflation

evidence.text: Which field excursions and scalar potentials can belong to an effective theory compatible with the conjectured quantum-gravity constraints?

sources.title: Infinite Distance Limits and Information Theory

evidence.text: What operational meaning does distance between quantum field theories have, why do infinite-distance endpoints arise, and can distinguishability provide a bottom-up motivation for the Swampland Distance Conjecture?

sources.title: Swampland distance conjecture, inflation and $\alpha$-attractors

evidence.text: Does every singularity at which an EFT loses degrees of freedom force its quantum-gravity cutoff to vanish? The authors distinguish finite-distance singularities with finitely many additional light states from infinite-distance limits involving an infinite tower.

sources.title: Infinite Distance Limits and Information Theory

evidence.text: Which observables, measurement limits, regulator choices, and complexity measures give a quantitative interpretation of infinite field distance?

sources.title: Emergence of Weak Coupling at Large Distance in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: What restrictions does quantum gravity impose on continuous parameters and asymptotic scalar-field geometry? The imported conjectures connect scalar expectation values, infinite moduli-space diameter, and towers becoming exponentially light with geodesic distance.

evidence.text: Which bound configurations of constituent Dirac monopoles form a unit-charge monopole of a surviving U(1), how can such configurations be assembled, and how does their internal gravitational stability bear on descent of magnetic WGC constraints?

evidence.text: Divide S < EL by E and insert the relativistic gas ratio S/E. This produces the lower size bound needed to test compatibility with the independently derived collapse upper bound.

evidence.text: Track gauge-boson mass eigenstates and the surviving charge lattice after Higgsing, then iterate the construction through a chain of Abelian gauge groups.

sources.title: Tensionless Strings and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Allocate excitation among factors in proportion to their positive indices, then control integer rounding. For Jacobi products this yields a candidate large-level charge, whose survival still requires a nonzero final coefficient.

sources.title: Spin-2 fields and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Determine nonlinear onset by comparing operators on a weak-field solution. This supplies the scale outside which separated-source force estimates are meaningful, while leaving the overlapping nonlinear problem unsolved.

sources.title: Swampland Variations on a Theme by KKLT

evidence.text: Separate the fluctuation, derive its warped eigenproblem and solve the radial boundary-value problem. Compare eigenmasses with the conifold-modulus mass using the same frame and volume dictionary.

sources.title: Emergent strings from infinite distance limits

evidence.text: Continue periods and use their ratios to identify the small-fiber endpoint. Interpret the continuation as a modular transformation or quotient monodromy; the complete three-fold implementation is imported.

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture for Noncommutative Field Theory

evidence.text: What weak-gravity restrictions follow for noncommutative U(1) gauge theories and scalar theories from the gravitational effects of their solitons, and under what conditions can these restrictions inform commutative theories?

sources.title: An Introduction to the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: What precisely does the Weak Gravity Conjecture assert, what evidence supports it, and what would it imply for string-consistent effective theories and axion inflation? This is a pedagogical review, rather than a new general proof.

sources.title: Aspects of non-local QED and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Assuming the weak gravity conjecture applies to the chosen non-local QED model, what constraints follow for charged neutrinos and their non-locality scales, and how does the softened electric force modify a force-based WGC formulation?

sources.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture and Emergence from an Ultraviolet Cutoff

evidence.text: What upper bounds on the quantum gravity cutoff follow from charged sLWGC towers for general gauge groups, and can simultaneous strong gauge and gravitational interactions explain emergence or imply the WGC?

sources.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture in Asymptotically Safe Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can running gravitational and electromagnetic couplings in asymptotically safe quantum gravity modify charged-black-hole extremality so that the Weak Gravity Conjecture emerges from ultraviolet renormalization-group behavior?

sources.title: Snowmass White Paper: Implications of Quantum Gravity for Particle Physics

evidence.text: Review how quantum-gravity consistency conditions constrain low-energy EFT and might inform strong CP, the weak scale, new gauge interactions and dark energy. The white paper explicitly does not guarantee that gravitational considerations solve these problems.
